selected.title: The rock goes in
selected.texas_link: NOV provides the existing Navasota test center for the proposed SMU mineral proving ground.

movement.actor: The United States Department of Energy
movement.action: selected a university proposal for award negotiations
movement.object: SMU Well-to-Mine Proving Ground in Navasota

selected.why_today: The September 9th federal selection and September 10th SMU account newly expose how an existing Texas drilling site could become a repeatable mining testbed.
selected.consequence: Students and workers would practice advanced mining techniques at a controlled test site; these are intended benefits and no completed trial is reported.
selected.application_change: Oilfield drilling, sensing and automation would be adapted for mining using engineered mineral-bearing rock placed in existing wells.
selected.counter_image: A proposed synthetic mine has no completed project test result in these announcements, and selection for award negotiations is not an operating facility.
selected.earned_take: Placing engineered rock underground creates a challenge the tools can face repeatedly before their usefulness is assumed.

agency.next_step: DOE and the project partnership must complete award negotiations and develop the proposed proving ground.
agency.who_can_act: DOE, SMU and the named project partners; no public comment window is published.

rejected.title: UT Physicians ambient documentation
rejected.reason: A genuine current adoption plan, but conversation-to-note graphics offer a weaker physical hook than the engineered-rock test.

rejected.title: UTA tutor and police training
rejected.reason: The primary research is useful but the classroom and police uses require separate evidentiary timelines that crowd this short film.
